docs.title: Transport
docs.text:
The latest version of the LCI model in the POLARIIS format is available here and on the Drive (CIRAIG_POLARIIS+\5.2 - Volet transport\4 - Modèles\Template)

This document aims to describe all sector-specific modelling, data and parameters. It also presents how the models are translated into the POLARIIS+ template.

This is Alexandre's simplified documentation version. To find Susie's version, which may cover more details : click here.

All modules and useful resources for the transport sector are available in the transport axis repo. The structure of the repo is the following :

Folder Main content / role G-drive/ Working exports and draft materials copied from Google Drive, including draft taxonomies and intermediate migration/QC files. taxonomy/ More finalized taxonomy work that is closer to POLARIIS template migration, including cleaned taxonomy tables and supporting references. However, following my works, it is the lastest template version that must be used for now. modules/ Sector-specific parameterization and modelling workflows. Current core modules include ttw_MJpervkm/, scope1_EF/, vehicle_component/, and fuel/. src/ Shared source assets for documentation and diagrams, including process-tree and workflow images. legacy/ Older scripts, exploratory work, and historical artifacts kept for traceability but not treated as the current implementation.

docs.title: Definition of the targeted studied system
docs.text: The targeted system is to model all road/air/water/rail transport system. As of the first version, it is focused on road transport vehicle system, with a focus on light-duty vehicles.

docs.title: Technological coverage / Object of study
docs.text: Three main modules have been treated with more or less granularity : - Vehicle manufacturing - Vehicle use - Fuel production

docs.title: Geographical coverage
docs.text: Primary fleet data grounding in current workflow is QC/Canada-oriented, including data sources from SAAQ, NRCAN etc., while many modelling parameters are designed as transferable by taxonomy dimension.

docs.title: Temporal coverage
docs.text:
Primary fleet data using most recent available data (e.g., 2024) from the obtainable data sources, other parameters, equations, and supporting notebooks also uses most up-to-date knowledge base, current modelling not designed for dynamic and/or prospective assessment though.

Impact category-wise, the database can support any impact characterization as inventory flows are inclusive (not just focusing on GHG).

docs.title: Functions and functional units
docs.text:
Primary function: - to provide transport service including both passenger and freight

Functional units (FU): - final FU: per vehicle-km (vkm), then allocated as person-km or tonne-km for passenger or freight, below are detailed reference flows for different modules: - vehicle use (scope 1) : emissions (mass) per vkm; - vehicle manufacturing : per one vehicle; - fuel production : emissions (mass) per MJ of fuel produced.

The ttw energy consumption module is used for scaling to the fuel module with a reference flow of MJ per vkm.

docs.title: Taxonomy and definitions
docs.text:
This module is built on the following object dimensions :

Space Dimensions Definition Vehicle Vehicle Class In Canada, the classification of vehicles is achieved on the basis of two quantitative criteria : the Gross Vehicle Weight Rate and the interior volume. Powertrain The power generator used in the vehicle. Vehicle ModelYear The year of the manufactured batch of the model (a same model can have slightly different properties through the years). Vehicle MakeModel The model of the vehicle. Vehicle GWVR The Gross Vehicle Weight Rating represents the maximum safe weight of a vehicle when fully loaded : it encompasses the curbmass of the vehicle and passengers and cargo weight. (This dimensions hasn't been used yet : it is yet to determine if it can be useful in the future.) Vehicle Component The main blocks on which is built the vehicle. Battery chemistry For BEVs and hybrid systems, the battery functions with a certain battery chemistry which can vary from a model to an other. Vehicle Subcomponent The most granular level of elements composing the vehicle yet : they can be seen as a recipe to build the Vehicle Component

This module is also built on the following action dimensions :

Space Dimensions Definition Vehicle Manufacturing Component Assembling Exclusively cover the fabrication of the Vehicle Component. Vehicle Assembling Covers the fabrication of the complete vehicle with the Vehicle Component. Marketing Component Covers the transportation of the Vehicle Component. Marketing Vehicle Covers the transportation of complete vehicle.

docs.title: Model and hypothesis
docs.text:
The complete vehicle is composed of three main Vehicle Component blocks : - Vehicle system - Energy storage system - Chassis&Body

Those Vehicle Component are themselves composed of Vehicle Subcomponent elements. The mass of those elements is defined in one of the two following ways : - Fixed Mass : the mass of the subcomponent takes a fixed value depending only the Vehicle Class and the Powertrain. - Specified Mass : the mass of the component is calculated based on the mass ratio of the subcomponent to the curbmass of the vehicle (the ratio depends on the Vehicle Class and the Powertrain).

The three Vehicle Component have the following "recipes" :

A. Vehicle system

The recipe depends on the Powertrain.

Powertrain Mass Calculation Subcomponent ICEV (-gasoline or -diesel) Fixed Mass Gearbox Specified Mass Combustion engine (full unit: block, head, moving parts and engine hardware) Exhaust system (post-combustion exhaust line and aftertreatment equipment) Transmission BEV Fixed Mass PDU (power distribution/protection high-voltage unit) Charger (on-board charging hardware) Converter Inverter (for motor control/regeneration) Specified Mass e-motor (traction electric machine) Transmission

B. Body&Chassis

The recipe depends on the Vehicle Class.

Vehicle Class Mass Calculation Subcomponent Light Duty Vehicle (excl. Pickup trucks) Specified Mass Glider (excl. tire&wheel) (non-propulsion body&chassis package used as a proxy dataset) Tires Wheels Pickup trucks Specified Mass Cabin Frame-Blanks-Saddle Suspension Tires&Wheels

C. Energy storage system

The recipe depends on the Powertrain. The mass calculation of the elements is different from the others. The mass of a battery is calculated based on the fraction of its Capacity (kWh) over its Specific energy (kWh/kg). The mass of a fuel tank is a proxy based on the fuel tank capacity (L) and a reference fuel tank (for which we have data on capacity and mass) : precise model is explained here

Powertrain Mass Calculation Subcomponent ICEV (-gasoline or -diesel) Mass Proxy Fuel Tank BEV Specified Mass Battery

Those recipes actually end up as Bills of Material for the fabrication of the Vehicle Component. No other resources than the Vehicle Subcomponents are used in the model.

All resources necessary for the assembling of the Vehicle Components and the vehicle itself are grouped in the final Assembling Vehicle process. Electricity, water and heat inputs are calculated based on the mass of the vehicle we are "building".

Location - location = unspecified for component-wise aggregation - downstream manufacturing is assumed in CA-QC where a location is required.

docs.title: From real life to POLARIIS+
docs.text:
The data for mass calculation/data of the parameters is all gathered in modules/vehicle_component/input_p_vehicle_component_v1.4.xlsx (here) (root source : premise, maybe others ?).

The fuel tank proxy is explained in modules/vehicle_component/fuel_tank_proxy/fueltank_readme.md (here)) (root source : model and assumptions by Alexandre).

The data for the mass of the models is gathered in modules/curbmass/model's curbmass and vehicle class/ready for use.xlsx (here are the explanations) (root source : SAAQ database, EPA website and calculations by Alexandre).

The data for the necessary input in Vehicle Assembling is gathered in modules/vehicle_component/vehicle_manuf/input_p_vehicle_manuf_v1.0.xlsx (here) (root source : premise).

Currently, no data has been found for the market activities.

docs.title: Gap analysis
docs.text:
In comparison with the ideal process tree : The vehicle manufacturing is partially covered. The "recipes" are implemented in a "3 layer model" : the Final Vehicle is built from 3 main Components, themselves built from Subcomponents. The Subcomponents production is provided directly by ecoinvent.

The vehicle distribution is partially covered. An attempt for a structure of market activities in the POLARIIS template has been done. However, without data, it is still difficult to realize if those processes are rightly designed. The key for transport data in markets may be found in vehicle manufacturing files. It provides excel-based dropdown automation with centroid-based total distance and modal split screening logic (NB : it is not yet a complete calibrated logistics model).

Detailed gap analysis in Susie's draft.

docs.title: Driving Vehicle (consumption and emissions)
docs.text: This section regroups two modules : - Tank-to-Wheel energy, - Scope 1 emissions.

docs.title: Taxonomy and definitions
docs.text:
This module is built on the following object dimensions :

Space Dimensions Definition Vehicle Vehicle Class In Canada, the classification of vehicles is achieved on the basis of two quantitative criteria : the Gross Vehicle Weight Rate and the interior volume. Powertrain The power generator used in the vehicle. Vehicle ModelYear The year of the manufactured batch of the model (a same model can have slightly different properties through the years). Vehicle MakeModel The model of the vehicle. Elementary Flow Substance_name The elementary substance (geography, unit and cross-cutting attributes stripped out). Substance_direction Emitted to vs extracted from the environment. Compartment Environmental medium, hierarchical. Roots: Air, Water, Soil_land, In_ground, Biotic. Energy EnergyType Source of power. Fuel for Transport Fuel origin route Where the fuel has been extracted. Deposit Type The type of deposit from which the fuel has been extracted. Production Method The production method of the fuel. Space Dimensions Definition All these dimensions revolve around one central action : Vehicle Driving Driving classic and daily-life road vehicles.

docs.title: Model and hypothesis
docs.text:
This activity is a auxiliairy activity providing a service for "1 vkm of driving".

Module ttw_energy

In order to get that service, we first need to determine how much energy input will be needed. This is the "tank-to-wheel energy". In our model, the energy input depends on the Vehicle Class and the Powertrain.

A linear regression for each Vehicle Class x Powertrain combination has given us the following equation (see here for a detailed explanation of the regression by Susie) :

\(\text{Tank-to-Wheel Energy} = \text{a * driving-mass + b}\)

with a the the slope of the linear regression in MJ of fuel / vkm / kg of Vehicle and b the intercept of the linear regression in MJ of fuel / vkm. (root source : Susie's works and carculator).

Module Scope 1

On the other hand, the outputs are exclusively Substance emissions in the biosphere (assumed in air). The emissions are calculated in three different ways : - specific equations for emission factors per MJ relying on fuel properties (CO2 and SO2) (root source : Fuel Effects on Exhaust Emissions from Onroad Vehicles in MOVES3) , - emission factors per MJ of fuel (CH4 and N20) (root source : "Table 5. GHG Emission Factors of Fuels", "Greenhouse Gas Emissions Quantification Guide February, 2025", environnement.gouv.qc.ca), - emissions factor per vkm driven (depending on the Powertrain and the Vehicle Class only / independant from Fuel Type) (for all other emited Substances), - some of those factor can be corrected depending on the Speed of the Vehicle (CO, NH3, NOx, PM2,5) (root source : MOVES).

Obviously, those Scope 1 substances are emitted only with ICEVs. Data on hybrid vehicles are yet to be added.

docs.title: Future progress
docs.text: • The next step for this module is to refine the adjusting factor for the tank-to-wheel consumption depending on the driving context.

docs.title: Fuel production
docs.text: The fuel module covers a 3 steps process tree that will be explained linearly.

docs.title: Taxonomy and definitions
docs.text:
This module is built on the following object dimensions :

Space Dimensions Definition Energy Energy Type Source of power (used both as energy inputs and as reference product objects). Fuel for Transport Fuel Status State of the fuel in the production chain. Deposit Type The kind of oil deposit from which the crude oil has been extracted. Production Method Child dimension for the parent dimension Deposit Type (Oil Sand & Cold Lake) Fuel Origin Route The deposit area from which the crude oil has been extracted. Fuel Infrastructure Required infrastrucutres along the production stage of fuel. Fuel Blending Bio-Ratio Bio-sourced fuel blending ratio (set at 0 for fuel type that aren't concerned). Elementary Flow Substance Name The elementary substance (geography, unit and cross-cutting attributes stripped out). Substance Direction Emitted to vs extracted from the environment. Compartment Environmental medium, hierarchical. Roots: Air, Water, Soil_land, In_ground, Biotic. Others Technosphere Ingredients Bunch of technosphere resources (not necessarly linked).

docs.title: Model and hypothesis
docs.text:
The current models and data cover the four following fuel profiles :

Energy Type Origin Route Deposit Type Production Method Motor Gasoline (conventional) Alberta, Canada Cold Lake dilbit Alberta, Canada Oil Sand SCO Canada (conventional) Conventional United-States (conventional) Convnetional Fischer-Tropsch Diesel (FTD 100) Alberta, Canada Cold Lake dilbit Alberta, Canada Oil Sand SCO Canada (conventional) Conventional United-States (conventional) Convnetional

Let's explore the fuel production route chronologically ! The precise list of flows can be found in the following files : - processes and reference units - precise flows

root source : iveo_QC_fuel.xlsx works by Susie

A. Extracting crude oil

That step only covers the extraction from Alberta : - Cold Lake dilbit, CA-AB - SCO Oil Sand, CA-AB

The "recipe" for oil extraction is quite similar in both cases (all flow depend on the type of fuel) :

Flow Type Ingredient Type Specified Ingredient Output Extracted Crude Oil Emissions (in biosphere) Flaring (carbon dioxide only). Venting (carbon dioxide and methane). Fugitive (carbon dioxide and methane). NRCAN (whole bunch of different substances). Input Crude Oil To Extract Energy Energy inputs (electricity, burned fuel). Services Water Treatment. Waste to be treated. Infrastructures On Shore Petroleum Field (unit). On Shore Well (km). Technosphere Ingredients

The different emission sources are separated to be tagged and identifiable in contribution analysis.

In this process it is assumed that there is no Oil Loss in the extraction process (the input and output values are equal).

In the data files, some reference output unit are in MJ (instead of kg) : the conversion has been made within the template.

B. Pipelining oil

The pipelining of crude oil is delt with accross two different activity : - one auxiliary activity ("market for transport of crude oil by pipeline") - one main activity ("market for crude oil")

The market for transport of crude oil by pipeline is an auxiliary activity providing the service for 1 tkm of crude oil transport.

The shadow flows represent the crude in Location A (input) and Location B (output). The real flows, taking root in ecoinvent, are : - A lenght fraction of Pipeline infrastructure - A market for electricity accross North America

It is assumed that the whole pipeline contributes to the transport of crude oil, even though the real path of crude oil is shorter. Thus, electricity from all accross the region is used.

The main activity calls for that service and is designed to transport one kilogram of crude oil. The only variable in this activity is the pipelining distance, which ends up defining "how much" of the service we are calling.

The oil input is provided by the template's extraction activity for Alberta Oil Sand and Cold Lake Oil, and provided directly by ecoinvent for conventional oil from USA and Canada.

C. Refining oil

The "recipe" for oil refining is similar for all cases (all flow depend on the type of fuel) :

Flow Type Ingredient Type Specified Ingredient Output Refined Fuel Emissions (in biosphere) Air/Water/Soil/Soil industrial all regrouped in the multiflow. Input Crude Oil Electricity Medium voltage. Biosphere Resources Water. Land. Natural Gas High pressure.

There are two recipes in the multiflow tab : one for conventional (US and Canada) oil and one for unconventional (OilSand and ColdLake) oil. Actually, both recipes are the exact same, but one more dimension is needed for OilSand and ColdLake oil, as they are paretn modality of the Production method dimension.

docs.title: Misunderstanding of self_to
docs.text:
Lou and I realized I mis-used the self_to parameter tag in the generic_activity tab for the pipelining activities (main and auxiliary).

Here is a list of small problems to fix : - [Pipelining auxiliary activity] : the two used parameters shouldn't even be self_to. They should be defined as self parameters. The pipelining_oil_elec_per_tkm could be renamed as market of electricity for pipelining with Energy Type = Medium voltage electricity x Location. - [Oil Loss flow in pipelining main activity] : there is a self_to(flow1, flow2). However, the parameter that is called does not depend on the "self flow" itself. That may be a new type of parameter to add.

En français pour être sur d'être clair sur ce point : D'un point de vue général, j'ai mal compris la signification de self/self_to. Je pensais que l'object_profile auquel on fait référence et le paramètre que l'on appelle devaient avoir exactement les mêmes dimensions de profil.

Par exemple, si mon flow a pour dimension Vehicle Class / Powertrain / MakeModel, je pensais que je ne pouvais appeler que les paramètres avec un tel obj1 (alors qu'en réalité je pouvais appeler tout paramètre dont les dimensions de l'obj1 sont inclues dans les dimensions de mon flow : ie je pouvais appeler un obj1 = Vehicle Class seulement).

Il se peut donc que certains profils de paramètres ou de flow soient "sur-spécifiés" par rapport à ce qui est nécessaire.
